headline: Organization is putting things where you can find them—external order that supports internal clarity
universal_truth: External order supports internal order; environment shapes mind
fun_facts: The average person spends 2.5 days per year looking for lost items
Clutter has been shown to increase cortisol (stress hormone) levels
The most organized people have systems, not just clean spaces—everything has a home
discussion_questions: What does your physical space say about your mental state?
What organizing system actually works for you?
What would better organization make possible?

hook.script: Where are your keys? Your important documents? That thing you need right now? Organization isn't just tidiness—it's a system that lets you find what you need when you need it. External order creates internal peace.

cliff.script: Some people seem naturally organized while others live in chaos. Is organization a personality trait you're born with, or a skill you can develop?

options.text: Organization is a skill built on systems—deciding where things go and consistently putting them there—anyone can learn it
options.response: Yes. Organized people have systems—'keys go here, bills go there.' The skill is creating and maintaining these systems. It's learnable, not innate.

options.text: Some people are just naturally better at keeping track of things
options.response: Natural tendencies vary, but organization fundamentally comes from systems, not personality...

fact1.title: Everything Has a Home
fact1.script: The secret of organized people: everything has a designated place. Keys go on the hook. Papers go in the file. When you finish using something, it returns home. Disorganization happens when things don't have homes—or don't go back.

fact2.title: Clutter and Stress
fact2.script: Research shows cluttered environments increase stress hormones. Visual noise competes for attention. Your brain processes everything in view. Physical clutter creates mental clutter. Cleaning your space can literally clear your mind.

fact3.title: Systems Over Willpower
fact3.script: Organization fails when it requires constant willpower. Succeed by making organization easy: put things where they naturally land, create routines that maintain order, use systems that work with your habits rather than against them.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: External order supports internal order. Organization teaches that environment shapes mind. Create systems that work—your future self will thank you.

outro.script: That's Day 186. Tomorrow, we'll explore paying attention on purpose—focus. Until then, give one homeless item in your space a permanent home.

growTrack.title: One Home - Reduce Finding Friction
growTrack.learning_objective: Create systems for commonly lost items
growTrack.activity: Choose one thing you frequently lose or search for. Give it a home—a specific place it always goes. Practice returning it there until it becomes automatic. One good system beats a hundred good intentions.
